text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the cited claims are accurate for their sentences. The summary is cautious in places and flags that no audit trail was received. But the conclusion is too strong given a mixed picture: the 99215 share is 2.21x expected (z 1.57), roughly 163 excess 99215 claims, and 18 low-complexity 99215 claims are listed on the card but none are cited or used. Only 17 of 298 99215 claims (about 6%) were documented, so 'do not pursue recovery' overreaches. The headline 'mostly support' is also odd with 0% below. Notes with unsupported 99214 (2 below billed) and 5 notes with data reviewed but no lab are mentioned only partly and not followed up. The investigator would have to redo the analysis of the low-complexity 99215 claims.","problems":["Recommends not pursuing recovery based on 17 documented 99215 claims out of 298 (about 6% sample), which is not representative","Ignores the 2.21x ratio to expected and ~163 excess 99215 claims when concluding a high-acuity panel; the headline and leaning dismiss an elevated signal","No cited low-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0097014, C0097919, C0098462 with 0-1 conditions), though 18 were on the card; the examples are selectively supportive","The 5 notes claiming moderate-plus data with no lab on the claim are mentioned but not followed up in next steps","Does not note the 2 documented 99214 claims below billed level (C0098108, C0098954) even though the provider's below-billed rate of 8.7% for 99214 is above peers","Next steps are generic and do not name specific documentation requests; the high-complexity patient share is not contrasted with the 0-1 condition 99215 share by numbers"]}
